title: Our warehouse tycoon built in Godot with Claude Code just got its Steam page, here's how the AI side actually went
author: flockbaygames
selftext:
Shelf-Made Tycoon is a cozy tycoon game about growing a tiny warehouse into a logistics empire. You start with one small building and not much money and every good deal you land turns into more space more clients and bigger ones, until trucks and trains and ships are all bringing work to your door. When money gets tight a local crime syndicate starts calling with big cash for a few unmarked crates \*cough cough\* but any one of their vans could be driven by an undercover cop and getting caught means losing everything. Even when it all runs smoothly it is oddly relaxing to just zoom in and watch it work

You can wishlist it here: [Shelf-Made Tycoon on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4325520/ShelfMade_Tycoon/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=coming_soon&utm_content=aigamedev).

Claude Code wrote the GDScript in Godot 4.7, about 34,000 lines and mostly on Opus. What made it hold up was the loop around the model more than the model itself, since every edit had to pass a parse check and a headless sim test and Claude could open the Godot editor and play the game to see what it built before calling anything done. Giving it that loop is the reason we built Flockbay, and the whole game was built on it.

The 3D models are not text-to-3D. The agent wrote the geometry in Blender from concept sheets we approved first, and the truck and forklift and cars were rebuilt when the first versions drifted from the sheets. The sound effects are AI-generated too, and the town and farmland and seasons are drawn at runtime by code and shaders.

Where the AI was weakest was taste. Our own playtest note on the first farmland was that it looked like AI slop and it took a full redraw with hedgerows and farm tracks and seasonal crops before it read as something a bit nicer to have as an cozy environment. Ask me anytihng about the workflow!

replies.author: karl_mainz
replies.body:
I found [Slopalytics](https://slopalytics.com/?hide-reasoning=max,none) to be the best for comparing the models. I like that it has cost and time per task not just per token, which is important as Astra tends to use fewer tokens to do the same work.

There's a tab to compare execution time too, as like high effort can be good but it can also take ages.

I think the best flow at the moment is to use Opus or Astra to fully plan out the project - not just a high level plan, but like down to the level of what actually has to be executed. Then use Sol or perhaps even Luna for execution.

Although Opus 5.5 has been incredible, it still seems like OpenAI has an advantage on those cheaper grunt-work models. 

There's also [Real API pricing](https://real-api-pricing.vercel.app) which is good for comparing the models under subscriptions (i.e. not API pricing).

replies.author: karl_mainz
replies.body:
Yeah it’s best to try and use Astra only to create plans. But sometimes creating the plan is still a lot of work as it requires investigation etc. and then this can still use up all your usage 🥲

Also the subscription is much more opaque - like at API pricing it seems Astra on high is the best value for money, using something like Sol for execution. But if they’ve nerfed their subscription plan usage compared to Anthropic then this won’t hold true for subscription users.

I still haven’t found a really good comparison of the subscriptions, the second link above uses token count, but this unfairly penalises models which use less tokens.

comments.author: CrimsonBolt33
comments.body:
I confused what you mean by the graphics were not text to 3d...as what you described sounds exactly like text to 3d lol.

What am I missing? Do you mean they weren't prompted "build me a car, no mistakes"?

replies.author: flockbaygames
replies.body: Text-to-3D usually means a tool that turns a prompt straight into a finished mesh, and we didn't use one. An image model drew a concept sheet we approved, then Claude wrote Blender Python that builds the truck part by part and checked its renders against the sheet, so each model is a normal .blend file with clean low poly geometry we can edit by hand.

replies.author: CrimsonBolt33
replies.body: ahh so text to image via specialized AI then image to model with Claude?

replies.author: flockbaygames
replies.body: Yes pretty much. The concept sheet came from an image model, then Claude studied it and wrote the Blender script that builds the model, rendering it and fixing whatever didn't match the sheet. Both steps ran on Flockbay, which we built so Claude could drive Blender and Godot like that.
